_comment: Player-facing tunables. Prices and city income are recovered from the 1990 manual and the executable (see `sources` below). Everything else here that was never recovered is a labelled stand-in the owner accepted or set, and meant to be changed by editing this file, not by editing code.

measured._comment: What the original actually does, measured in DOSBox on 2026-11-12 (T-008). These are reference numbers, not the values the server runs on: `roundSeconds` and `speeds` above are a deliberate deviation for browser playability and are labelled as such in sources.speeds and notes.speeds. Evidence: docs/re/MOVEMENT.md, probe scripts in the T-008 notes directory.

pieceTable._comment: Addresses the original's per-piece pass indexes, read off the loop (decompiled.c 4381-4595) and dumped live 2026-11-12. DS-relative. The pass walks the 0..99 visit order, then indexes parallel per-unit arrays by the record number - there is no 16-byte unit record.

passRatePerRound._comment: AC3 (T-008): piece-pass wraps counted over a FULL round, not the 8 s sampler (11 wraps per 129.2 s round at speed 1, 16 at speed 3, 63-64 at speed 6; no pass at speed 0). Source: docs/re/MOVEMENT.md, AC3.

cellsPerRoundByKind._comment: AC3 table (PM 3495 item 1). Every row is keyed on the STATIC per-kind allowance byte[0x19a6 + kind] (measured.pieceTable.kindAllowance above), never on a kind identity read from 0x906 - Q35 is open. status: MEASURED = a full-round run exists and evidenceRef names it; MEASURED-HARNESS = the run exists but the harness wrote the kind nibble (PM 3481 item 2 accepts it as measuring the rule); PREDICTED = the static byte only, NO RUN: the row is (byte/20) steps per pass x the measured passes per round, a prediction and not evidence. cellsPerRound values are [low, high] cells in one 129.2 s round at that speed. Kinds 0, 3 and 4 carry a zero byte and cannot move in a pass at all; the server does not run on these numbers - move.cellsPerRound above is still the runtime table.

0.note: unused slot, zero byte; nothing moves without a budget

3.note: transport; zero byte, it moves as cargo

4.note: zero byte, no kind 4 on any checked start board

5.note: no run: predicted from byte 36; the 36-allowance band measured on kind 6 is 1.64-1.81 cells/pass, and 1.00 if the piece is land-capped at one visit per pass

7.note: no run: predicted from byte 40 (2.0 steps/pass), 1.00 if the piece is land-capped

8.note: no run: predicted from byte 40 (2.0 steps/pass), 1.00 if the piece is land-capped

9.note: no run: predicted from byte 40 (2.0 steps/pass), 1.00 if the piece is land-capped

cellsPerRound.source: STAND-IN, UNMEASURED (orderings only: Manual p.9 tank at most 2x infantry; p.21 sea faster than land, transports slightly slower than other ships). No per-round cell rate was ever printed.

sources.speeds: MEASURED 2026-11-12 (T-008, docs/re/MOVEMENT.md): the original's round clock is 7646 units at 1/64 s each, i.e. 119.5 s of nominal game time, and it counts down at the same rate at every speed 0-6 (59.16 units/s in DOSBox 0.74-3 at 3000 cycles, so 129.2 s of wall clock; 3 legs per speed, 0/1/3/6). Every speed setting therefore has the SAME round length; the speed control paces piece and combat animation, not the round. Speed 0 stops piece movement dead (0 piece steps in 8 s) while the round clock still runs. DELIBERATE DEVIATION: `roundSeconds` and `speeds` above are not these numbers. They are the owner's 5 s round and 0/5/3.5/2.4/1.6/1/0.6 ramp, kept so a browser war lasts minutes rather than the original's two-hour campaign. The stand-in ordering (higher speed = shorter round) is contradicted by the original and is kept on purpose, pending a PM ruling; nothing outside this file treats it as recovered.
sources.move: cellsPerRound: STAND-IN, UNMEASURED for the per-kind numbers. Orderings only - tank > infantry and no more than 2x (p.9), ship > transport > infantry (p.21). MEASURED 2026-11-12 (T-008): the war room walks all 100 pieces in one pass and the pass rate is 7.37/s at speed 1, 12.25/s at speed 3 and 49.23/s at speed 6, with 0 steps at speed 0, so a unit under orders can advance at most one cell per pass - about 9.5, 15.8 and 63.7 cells in one 119.5 s round at speeds 1/3/6 before its per-kind budget (DS:0x6FE against DS:0x1976) throttles it. The per-kind split was NOT captured (no unit could be put under orders in the driven walk), so no per-kind number is sourced. The map's own path costs (DS:0x011C, docs/re/RULES.md section 1) are recovered facts and live in rules.mjs, not here.

maxStrength.source: UNMEASURED (scale only; the manual shows a bar, p.20)

shotEveryRounds.source: DELIBERATE DEVIATION, pacing (D-017): the original fires every pass while in contact (docs/re/COMBAT.md s7), and a pass is speed-dependent; 2 is the manual's p.22 sentence kept as the browser pacing choice, awaiting Shane's ruling.

baseDamage.source: MEASURED FALLBACK ONLY (T-009, gate 3557 item 2): the runtime reads the 9x9 pairing matrix at measured.combat.damageMatrix.rows, indexed attackerKind*9 + targetKind, so tank->infantry is 26 from cell 2->1 and not this row's 20. These per-kind values remain only for a kind the matrix has no row for (nothing the eras field: infantry/tank/submarine/cruiser/carrier, of which only kinds 1/2/7/8/9 have rows). The old per-attacker collapse is gone; no pairing reads this object.
baseDamage.evidenceRef: docs/re/COMBAT.md s2; notes/t009/tables.py (2026-11-13); live duels 3 repeats each

flankMultiplier.source: MEASURED (T-009b, live leg): flank 1.5 is no longer disassembly-only. Three-piece layout so the defender is fighting a third piece (its target link is not the attacker), attacker facing perpendicular to the defender: tank vs entrenched infantry read 30 against the 20 matrix cell on repeats 2 and 3; repeat 1 read 20 with the facing byte re-pinned that pass, and that reading is kept in the log. The same geometry with matched facings reads 40 (rear x2). decompiled.c 7064-7071.
flankMultiplier.evidenceRef: docs/re/t009b/flank-2026-11-13.txt (repeats 2 and 3: dmg 30; repeat 1: 20, logged); docs/re/COMBAT.md s11

rearMultiplier.source: MEASURED (T-009): rear 2.0 when the attacker and the defender face the same way (the attacker is behind the defender), decompiled.c 7066-7069, only for land-vs-land and only while the defender is fighting another piece. Live: 40 against a 20 baseline.
rearMultiplier.evidenceRef: docs/re/COMBAT.md s2.2; live rear hit 40 v 20 (2026-11-13)

entrenchDamageFactor.source: MEASURED (T-009): must stay 1. The entrenchment discount is the kind-3 column of the damage matrix (20 -> 15 against infantry, 26 -> 20 against tanks), which the runtime now reads by giving an entrenched infantry defender code 3. A separate 0.75 would count the entrenchment twice, and it cannot express both 0.75 and 0.77 anyway. Terrain cover is a separate, unwired modifier (T-009b).
entrenchDamageFactor.evidenceRef: docs/re/COMBAT.md s4; damage matrix cells 1->3 and 2->3

entrenchRounds.source: DISASSEMBLY (T-009): the original has no entrench timer. The kind flips on the first eligible pass (stationary, no target, dig-in terrain) and reverts when a move is ordered (decompiled.c 9287-9290, 4523-4525). One round is the smallest value this key can carry.

landEngageCells.source: MEASURED (T-009): land engagement is dist^2 <= 5 in the 0x1956 matrix (FUN_188b_0216 squares the distance), which reaches (2,1) and not (2,2) - two cells.

seaRangeCells.source: MEASURED (T-009): the same matrix, classes 2/3/4 for kinds 7/8/9, thresholds 5/10/17 squared = 2/3/4 cells. Also matches Manual p.24 (sub 2) and p.42 (sub < cruiser < carrier). A submarine cannot engage land at all (0).
seaRangeCells.evidenceRef: docs/re/COMBAT.md s3 and s11; live ladder docs/re/t009b/range-sub-cruiser-carrier-2026-11-13.txt (sub d2=4 fire, d2=9 no; cruiser d2=9 fire, d2=16 no; carrier d2=16 fire, d2=25 no)

attritionPerRound.source: STAND-IN, UNMEASURED as a per-round rate. The original applies attrition PER PASS from the 0x1996 table (desert/jungle 3, polar 5, lake 3, wasteland 34 with destruction, city-base-capital-dock 20 through the site branch, floor at strength 20). Passes per round depend on speed, so no single per-round number exists until D-017 is ruled. Reference rows: measured.combat.attritionPerPass.

attritionFloor.source: MEASURED (T-009): the code's floor is literally min(amount, strength - 20) (decompiled.c 9089-9093), and 20 of the 100 bar is p.21's 20 %.
attritionFloor.evidenceRef: docs/re/COMBAT.md s5 and s11; live floor docs/re/t009b/attr-lake-floor-2026-11-13.txt (lake 22 -> 20, then flat for the rest of a 30 s window)

repairPerRound.source: STAND-IN as a per-round rate. Measured: +10 per eligible pass, every other pass, on an own site whose terrain is docks/capital/base/city/oilfield, clamped at 100 (live leg 40 -> 50). Per-round depends on the speed, so it stays a reference row: measured.combat.repairPerPass.

airStrikeLandFactor.source: DISASSEMBLY (T-009); live leg UNMEASURED (T-009b). The strike deals (strength >> 1) + 1, so 100 leaves 49 - one point under half (decompiled.c 8795-8814). The runtime carries the manual's 0.5 because the module rounds a half-bar to 50; the exact 49 is recorded in measured.combat.airStrike.
airStrikeLandFactor.evidenceRef: docs/re/COMBAT.md s6 and s11 (air strike stays code-only); air-strike handler 1ac5:0dbe; live attempt docs/re/t009b/air-2026-11-13.txt, docs/re/t009b/air-burst-2026-11-13.txt

airStrikeSeaAmount.source: DISASSEMBLY (T-009) for hulls kind 5-7, still code-only after the T-009b live attempt: 34 per strike, three strikes on a full bar. MANUAL-CONTRADICTED, Manual p.25: kinds 8 and 9 (cruiser, carrier) lose 25 per strike = FOUR strikes, not the page's 'three strikes sink a ship'. FUN_1ac5_0dbe @ 1ac5:0dbe, 8795-8814 picks the constant by kind (34 for kind<8, 25 for 8/9). The code governs the port (room 3544 ruling 1); recorded in measured.combat.airStrike.manualContradiction.
airStrikeSeaAmount.evidenceRef: docs/re/COMBAT.md s6, s9.3 and s11; air-strike handler 1ac5:0dbe 8795-8814; live attempt docs/re/t009b/air-ship-2026-11-13.txt (no strike landed; see measured.combat.value.airStrike.liveLeg)

bombardFloor.source: Manual p.42, UNMEASURED. The original's real shore-fire rule is different and measured: a ship beyond 2 cells caps damage at (target strength - 30), halved when that cap is under 25 (decompiled.c 7082-7093). Recorded in measured.combat.modifiers.

militiaDamage.source: MEASURED (T-009b, live leg): standing on an enemy-owned site costs 2 strength per pass and pins the piece (move points to -10); an unowned site costs 20 per pass, floored at strength 20, until the capture lands (decompiled.c 9056-9077). One number cannot carry both, so this is the enemy-city value and the neutral value is in measured.combat.militia.
militiaDamage.evidenceRef: docs/re/t009b/militia-2026-11-13.txt (enemy 100->98 = 2; unowned 100->80 = 20; own site 0 damage); docs/re/COMBAT.md s11

pinRounds.source: STAND-IN, UNMEASURED, and with no original counterpart: contact is re-evaluated every pass, so the original pins only while an enemy is in range and has no duration to measure (docs/re/COMBAT.md s7).

damageMatrix._comment: DS:0x18f0, index targetKind + attackerKind*9. Row 0 overlaps the string tail 'ly = %d.' and kind 0 is an empty slot, so row 0 is never read. Dumped live 2026-11-13 and identical in CHQ_unpacked.EXE (file offset 0x341a0; the row stride 9 is confirmed against every row). This table IS the runtime: combatRules() builds it from these rows and baseDamageFor() indexes attacker*9+target; an entrenched infantry defender is looked up as kind 3 (the entrench column), not as a multiplier. Column 0 is a real byte, not padding: it is what the original reads when the TARGET is kind 9 (carrier), because a*9+9 is the next row's column 0. kindNineColumn is that row, byte for byte.
damageMatrix.runtimeWiring: attacker*9+target, kinds by name from this block's kinds map; defender kind 3 when kind === infantry && entrenched === true; target kind 9 reads kindNineColumn[attacker] (the next row's column 0); flank/rear read the attacker's facing against the defender's (same facing = rear x2, not-opposite = flank x1.5) and only while the defender is fighting a third piece.
damageMatrix.kindNineColumnSource: table byte a*9+9 in CHQ_unpacked.EXE at 0x341a0: attacker 1/2/3 -> next row col0 = 35, 4 -> 0, 5/6 -> 5, 7/8 -> 34, 9 -> 0x341fa = 25. A carrier as the target is therefore hit for 35 by infantry/tanks, 34 by subs/cruisers and 25 by another carrier; the table simply has no in-row column for kind 9.

rangeMatrix._comment: DS:0x1956, row = attacker range class, column = target class, values are SQUARED distance thresholds; column 5 is reused as the piece's own contact range. DS:0x194c maps kind to class: 0-4->0, 5-6->1, 7->2, 8->3, 9->4, 10-11->5.
rangeMatrix.status: MEASURED (T-009b, live): start-of-fire read off the target strength with the shooter pinned. Sub fires at d2=4 and not d2=9; cruiser at d2=9 and not d2=16; carrier at d2=16 and not d2=25.

modifiers.terrainCoverCityFormula: dmg - (dmg+1)/3 for defender kinds 1/3; dmg - dmg/5 for kind 2 (decompiled.c 7056-7062)
modifiers.terrainCoverStatus: MEASURED (T-009b, live): a tank hitting an entrenched infantry on a city terrain byte read 13 where the same pairing on open plain read 20, twice each. Cover is a SEPARATE modifier applied before flank/rear, not a second entrenchment: 20 - (20+1)/3 = 13.
modifiers.shipVsLandBeyondTwoCells: cap = targetStrength - 30, halved when the cap is under 25

attritionPerPass._comment: Manual p.21 AGREES with this list (desert, jungle, polar, lake, city, base, capital, dock); the amounts are what is new, and wasteland 34 is the one terrain the page does not list. Corrected per PM 3557: the interim 3543 'wasteland-only' reading was the branch that destroys, not the whole table.
attritionPerPass.status: PART MEASURED (T-009b, live): lake 3 and polar 5 per pass, no shooter, and the 20 floor holds (lake 22 -> 20, then flat). Desert DID NOT FIRE in three live runs (stationary at 100, stationary at 22, move points held at 16 on an isolated desert cell): the 0x1996 byte 35 = 0x23 carries the dig-in bit 0x20, and the per-pass handler did not damage it. Wasteland 34 is UNMEASURED: the 1942 board has no wasteland cell (0 of 43,520 nibbles in data/tmap.bin), and forcing 0x836=14 on an isolated cell produced no loss in 25 s while the plain control produced none either. The two entries that DID fire carry no flag bits; both that did not carry 0x20/0x10. Those are live contradictions of the table-as-per-pass reading and are reported, not changed. Jungle shares desert's byte and was not run.

attritionTable._comment: DS:0x1996 per terrain, bit 0x80 = through the combat path, 0x20 = dig-in terrain, low 5 bits = amount. Terrains 0-14: ocean, docks, ocean, lake, capital, base, city, oilfield, plain, forest, mountain, desert, jungle, polar, wasteland.

repairPerPass.units: +10 per eligible call of FUN_1c0d_0656; the 0xcae bit-3 toggle skips every other call, so 5 per pass averaged over two calls and about 59 per round at speed 1 (11.75 passes/round, T-008). Per round moves with speed, so only the per-call figure is a measurement and the per-round figure is arithmetic; the runtime's repairPerRound stays STAND-IN until D-017.

airStrike.manualContradiction: MANUAL-CONTRADICTED, Manual p.25: 'three strikes sink a ship' holds for kinds 5-7 (34 each) but not for kinds 8/9 (cruiser, carrier, 25 each = four strikes). FUN_1ac5_0dbe @ 1ac5:0dbe, 8795-8814. Code governs the port (room 3544 ruling 1).
airStrike.liveLeg: Event dispatch identified: event code 7 in the far-pointer table at DS:0x1a68 is FUN_1ac5_0dbe (offset 0x0dbe in the relocated segment 0x0c66). Requests are 5 bytes in a 40-byte ring at DS:0xefbc, write pointer DS:0xe940, read pointer DS:0xe42a. Live attempt: two queued code-7 events against a land target were consumed (wp/rp 0->5->10) with the target unchanged at 100; two against a sub were consumed (wp/rp 10->15->20) with the sub unchanged at 100; a 30 s burst of 200 injected events landed nothing. The handler gates on FUN_1ac5_1206 (nearest ENEMY aircraft within 3 cells) then FUN_1ac5_1156, whose result depends on the random at 0x148a, so the damage call is not reached from an injected event. Next step: drive the real air-strike UI command (the map-click handler FUN_1ac5_0390 pushes this same code-7 event), or stage an enemy aircraft record that survives the pass loop, then read the 34 / 25 / (s>>1)+1 deltas.

militia.floor: none on the enemy-site branch (2 can kill); 20 floor on the neutral branch, min(amount, strength-20)

entrench.trigger: stationary pass, no target, terrain bit 0x20
entrench.status: MEASURED (T-009b, live): one tank hit a red infantry as kind 1 for 26 (cell 2->1) and, after the defender entrenched to kind 3 on plain, hit the same piece for 20 (cell 2->3); the flip came on an eligible pass after the target was cleared

liveLegs._comment: T-009b, 2026-11-13, DOSBox 0.74-3 on the live 1942 board (speed 2). Every leg re-pinned position, terrain byte and target link each 60 ms and logged every strength delta with the pieces linking to the victim. Harness: docs/re/t009b/harness/ (self-contained; run as root for /proc/<pid>/mem).
liveLegs.flank: MEASURED: 30 (x1.5 of 20), 2 clean repeats; a matched-facing repeat of the same layout read 40 (x2).
liveLegs.entrenchPair: MEASURED: 26 as kind 1, 20 as kind 3, same attacker, same cell.
liveLegs.cover: MEASURED: city terrain byte 13 vs open plain 20, 2 repeats each; cover is separate from entrenchment.
liveLegs.attrition: PART MEASURED: lake 3 and polar 5 per pass with no shooter; the 20 floor holds (lake 22 -> 20, then flat). Desert lost nothing in three runs - a live contradiction, reported not changed; see attritionPerPass.status.
liveLegs.militia: MEASURED: enemy site 2, unowned site 20, own site 0.
liveLegs.airStrike: UNMEASURED: event path located and exercised, no damage landed; see airStrike.liveLeg.
liveLegs.q38: OPEN: a 60 s full-board strength scan at 30 ms on the crowded 1942 board logged 0 deltas and 0 unattributed deltas (0x89e, attributed by the 0xbde target links), so the 2-5 point loss did not reproduce in that state. Method and next step are the ones Q38 already names: the crowded trio with the pass counter and per-pass deltas on every record, sampled at a turn resolution rather than after it.

measured.source: MEASURED/DISASSEMBLY (T-009 2026-11-13, extended by T-009b 2026-11-13): reference rows for the numbers the runtime cannot carry yet. docs/re/COMBAT.md holds the addresses, call sites and contradictions with the manual.
measured.evidenceRef: docs/re/COMBAT.md; docs/re/t009b/README.md (T-009b legs and harness); DOSBox 0.74-3 cycles=auto, film_mode 0x1478 and 0xc8cc zeroed

notes.roundSeconds: 5 s chosen 2026-11-06 by the owner, and a DELIBERATE DEVIATION: the original's round is 119.5 s of game time and does not shorten with speed (measured 2026-11-12, T-008; see `measured` above and docs/re/MOVEMENT.md). At 1 cell per round the Washington-Moscow march is ~104 cells, about 8.7 minutes. The original felt like a campaign, not a 24-second war, and 0.14 s made income land every 3.5 s.
notes.payEvery: Rounds between income payments. 1: a city pays every round (Manual p.27).
notes.prices: Manual p.28 lists these in billions. config stores the manual's billions; rules.priceOf() converts with money.perBillion and returns integer millions so no float drifts. The sub/cruiser/carrier row order comes from the p.28 icons and is UNVERIFIED until a DOSBox capture.
notes.cityIncome: Manual p.27: each city produces 50 million (0.05 billion) per round. Kept as integer millions so 3 cities x 10 rounds is exactly 1500.
notes.capitalPays: UNVERIFIED. The current code has never paid a capital, and the manual names only cities; this flag keeps that behaviour explicit. Set true to make a capital pay like a city.
notes.startPool: Opening cash per era, in billions, for the player's own side. From Monitor Four on the running original (Manual p.27; renderer FUN_3711_16a8 @ 3711:16a8 divides DS:0x148e by 0x28 at 3711:16f3), captured per era in docs/captures/startmoney-<era>-blue-monitor4-own.png and written up in docs/re/START_MONEY.md. 1918 10, 1942 50, 1986 50, 2023 600. 9999 is UNVERIFIED (memory read only) and is a deliberate stand-in. Red has no capture of its own: red is given the Blue value on purpose (a recorded stand-in) rather than an invented number.
notes.handicap: OPPONENT'S STARTING MONEY (Manual p.17: 'you are allowed to adjust the amount of money with which your opponent begins the game... a handicapping device'). It is the opponent's pool only, never the player's: 1942 proves it, where the player starts with 50b and the spinner default is 030 (30b). Per-era defaults are stored because they are not constant (010 in 1918, 030 in 1942). 2023 has no spinner (null). Range 0-999 step 1 is an UNVERIFIED inference from the three digit columns; wrap behaviour is unknown. 1986's default and the ???? default are stand-ins, labelled in sources.handicap.
notes.rosters: Manual p.16. 1918 has no air power, tanks or carriers; 1942 adds them; 1986 adds nukes, aid, satellites and intel. 2023 uses the 1986 set. 9999 is UNVERIFIED and uses the 1986 set.
notes.speeds: The seven slot lengths for speeds 0-6, in seconds per round. All seven numbers are the owner's playability ramp (speed 1 = the old 5 s round, speed 6 = a hundred rounds a minute) and are a DELIBERATE DEVIATION from the original, which was measured on 2026-11-12 to run one 119.5 s round at every speed 0-6 and to make speed 0 a full stop for pieces but not for the round clock (T-008, docs/re/MOVEMENT.md). Index 0 keeps the original's 'time does not pass' meaning for pieces. A room carries its own speed and either seat may change it; both seat views see the number.
notes.move: cellsPerRound is the number of cells a kind may enter in one round. STAND-IN, UNMEASURED: only the manual's orderings are binding (tank up to 2x infantry, p.9; sea faster than land and transports slightly slower than other ships, p.21). The walker's route test uses the archive's own DS:0x011C cost bytes, which are recovered, not tuned, and stay in rules.mjs.
notes.fuel: STAND-IN. The archive's fuel reserve and burn were never recovered: 10000 reserve and 1 per round are invented and are here only so a side can run short. Per side, deliberately not the desktop archive's single shared reserve.
notes.steel: STAND-IN, an owner-designed expansion and not a recovery: the 1990 game had oil only. 40 held and 1 a round are invented so a second kind can be held and consumed. No yield is set on purpose: the archive never recovered one, so the server refuses to hand out steel rather than guess a number. Gated to 1942 and 1986; the other scenarios do not carry it.
notes.combat: T-003 replaces the desktop archive's stand-in fight (after HITS shots the defender is gone) with the manual's strength model (p.20-25). Every key in `combat` carries its own source. A value marked STAND-IN, UNMEASURED is a working number the owner may replace, not a recovered one; the combat panel says 'unmeasured' for those. Damage removes a unit only when a hit meets or exceeds its remaining strength (p.23). Relatives the manual states are kept: tank > infantry, entrenched takes less, flank takes more, sub < cruiser < carrier range.
notes.air: The 8 and 4 are the booklet counts (docs/POLISH_LOOP.md: air mission inactive 8 rounds, scramble 4). The reach of 10 is a STAND-IN: the archive's aircraft range was not recovered.
notes.nukes: A nuke is refused by default and the archive's own stand-in deals no damage and paints no wasteland. exclusion 2 is a STAND-IN guard around a capital; the archive kept a home-ground guard but never printed its size. The launch limit (three fired or three absorbed) is the booklet count and stays in code.
notes.overrun: Overrun is the tank's (Manual p.9): an ordered tank that meets enemy infantry in the next cell fights through it, taking losses, and enters the cell and continues if the infantry is destroyed. There is no count-based instant removal. The losses are `combat.baseDamage` for both sides.
notes.placement: STAND-IN. The archive printed where a purchase goes - land and air in any friendly city or base, ships only on docks - and the owner widened it: land and air anywhere in your own zone, ships into coastal water. Neither reach was ever printed, so 8 cells from a site you hold and 4 cells from a land cell are invented to make the rule exist. Change them here; the server refuses and the page highlights from this same block.
